chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The wine drinker will come on the Day of Resurrection with a blackened face, a bent side, a drooping tongue, calling out, 'The thirst! The thirst!'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs of a wine drinker on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the corporeal manifestation of spiritual decay, where the drinker’s distorted posture and blackened face reflect the internal corruption of the soul. The perpetual cry of 'Thirst' serves as a poignant eschatological irony, symbolizing the soul's unquenchable longing for divine proximity after being deprived of it through the consumption of wine. This description aligns with Shia exegetical traditions that view physical ailments in the afterlife as direct reflections of specific sins committed in the worldly life.
